## PHILIPPINES — profile (page 207)

- Header facts: Region: East Asia & Pacific; income group: Upper-middle-income; lending category: IBRD; data status: Data as reported (A); population: 116.8 million; GNI: 559,930; unit line: US$ million, unless otherwise indicated.
- Total external debt stock 2025: 147,175; change from 2024: +7.6%.

- Figure 1 Total external debt, 2015–25: 79,698 in 2015 and 147,175 in 2025. The line dips slightly after 2015, then rises steadily through the period, with faster gains in the later years, reaching its peak in 2025. Unlabeled intermediate points are approximately: a small decline to ≈2016–17, then increases from ≈2018 onward.

- Figure 2 External debt by creditor and creditor type in 2025, including IMF credit and SDR allocations:
  - Total external debt: 147,175
    - Public & publicly guaranteed: 93,713
    - Private nonguaranteed: 33,228
    - Short-term: 20,233
  - Public & publicly guaranteed — by creditor type: 93,713
    - Multilateral: 40,666
    - Bilateral: 11,359
    - Private creditors: 41,688
  - Multilateral: 40,666
    - Asian Dev. Bank: 17,480
    - World Bank-IBRD: 16,139
    - Other multilateral: 7,047
  - Bilateral: 11,359
    - Japan: 8,828
    - France: 1,293
    - Other bilateral: 1,237

- Figure 3 Debt ratios, 2015–25:
  - External debt / exports: 111%; change: +0.1%. Trend: broadly stable overall, with a dip in the earlier years and a modest recovery, ending near the top of its recent range.
  - External debt / GNI: 26%; change: +0.2%. Trend: slight decline early on, then gradual increase and stabilization by 2025.
  - Debt service / exports: 11%; change: -23.8%. Trend: volatile; sharp early drop, low mid-period levels, some rebound, then a decline by 2025.
  - Debt service / GNI: 3%; change: -23.7%. Trend: fluctuating at low levels; early drop, modest ups and downs, then lower again in 2025.

- Figure 4 Average terms on new commitments from official and private creditors, 2025:
  - Official creditors: maturity 26 yrs; grace period 8 yrs; interest rate 3.3%.
  - Private creditors: maturity 16 yrs; grace period 16 yrs; interest rate 3.2%.

- Notes: Shaded band shows the 25th–75th percentile range of DRS reporting countries.
- Source: World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database.
